reason: Two actual OSP/DST trials passed OpenStitch software checks but were rejected after direct visual inspection: wave foam still a single light mass, storm cloud too angular, no Turner-like sea motion. Stopped after two variants without meaningful artistic improvement.
method: Reconstructed semantic tower/lantern, boat/sails, clouds and water from the unchanged original; six manually defined independent wave families; per-family source luminance extracted irregular foam shapes. Two variants use independent extraction from the immutable original, but share the same hand-built structural map. Actual CLI new/apply/render/check/inspect/diagnose/fidelity/density/osp2dst/stats. All objects have explicit stitch type and tatami direction.

attempts.visual: Large bright foam masses still dominate and look flat; wave peaks angular; boat and lighthouse identifiable.
More selective foam threshold; slightly fewer pale masses but still reads as flat geometric surf, not pictorial turbulence.

fidelity.reason: No source image embedded in vector OSP

artistic_self_critique: Both versions fail visual gate A/D: clouds too angular, foam flattened into bright patches and the waves lack curved direction and negative spaces. V2 only improves numerical density, not visual fidelity.
changes: 2 source-based foam threshold variants, with hand-built lighthouse/ship/cloud semantic polygons
Produced actual editable OSP, corresponding DST, preview, segmentation and native diagnostics
No changes to main or benchmark manifest
lessons: Semantic shape design must improve before tuning stitch density; source-luminance segmentation inside manually defined wave families still merges foam into large blocks.
Use non-overlapping water/foam negative-space masks and non-angular cloud geometry next.
